newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-MORE BIG NAMES TUMBLE AT ALL ENGLAND CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-MORE BIG NAMES TUMBLE AT ALL ENGLAND CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: More big names fell by the wayside at the All England badminton championships on Wednesday, led by former finalist and ex-world champion Joko Suprianto.
The Indonesian exited in the second round to Dane Peter Ramussen, who won fairly comfortably 15-10 15-3.
Suprianto's defeat followed that of compatriot and former Olympic champion Allan Budi Kusuma who was beaten in a first-round match which ended after midnight on Tuesday in a virtually deserted arena.
Kusuma lost a protracted battle to another Indonesian, Gopi Chand, 12-15 15-10 15-13, effectively ending his hopes of ever winning this prestigious title.
The same probably applies to Thomas Stuer-Lauridsen, a bronze medallist in Barcelona in 1992 when Kusuma won the gold.

The Dane lost his first-round match in straight games and his country's main hopes lay once again with Atlanta gold medallist Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen, who safely reached the third round on Wednesday with a business-like 15-2 15-8 defeat of China's Xie Yangchun.
Hoyer-Larsen is seeking his third All England title in succession, ahead of the world championship in Scotland in May.
His predecessor as All England winner, Heryanto Arbi of Indonesia, the reigning world champion, survived a second-round scare before quelling 20-year-old Mark Constable 10-15 15-10 15-9.

In the women's singles, top seed Mia Audina of Indonesia breezed past Japan's Hisako Mizui 11-5 11-1, while Suzi Susanti, a four-time winner here, took just 18 minutes to overcome young Emma Chaffin of England, 11-1 11-1.
